newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks higher, seen extending gains.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks higher, seen extending gains.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly higher with new records on Tuesday on stronger volume and were seen as extending gains due to continuing investor interest.
"Foreign investors are buying actively," said Josko Milisa of consultancy and brokerage I.F.C. He cited seaside hoteliers as the best possible gainers in the medium-term.
* Seven of 11 stocks rose, two fell and two were unchanged.
* Most actively traded Podravka, with 12,217 shares sold, gained 15 kuna to 250, after peaking at a historic high of 265 during the session.
* The biggest gainer in absolute terms, confectioner Kras, added 40 kuna to 510 selling 1,590 units.
* Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka rose 30 kuna to a new high of 930 kuna on volume of 5,208.
* Drugs firm Pliva was up 400 kuna to 13,500, but it only sold 29 shares. The company reported a strong first-half profit rise on Monday.
* Electric cables maker Elka rose 25 to 185 kuna with 69 shares sold.
* Hotelier Laguna, with 487 shares, was up to 900 from 880 kuna, having also touched a new 910-kuna high.
* Jadranturist firmed two kuna to 232, selling 1,925 units.
- Riviera by 10 kuna to 105 on volume of 392 shares and
- Arenaturist by five to 100 kuna on volume of 200.
* Dalmatian hotels Suncani Hvar stock unchanged at 45 kuna with 1,478 shares sold.
* Croatia Banka, trading 50 shares, also flat at 135 kuna from two months ago.
* Volume up at a record 23,649 units, turnover 9.9 million kuna.
* Central bank's exchange rate: 5.3993 kuna = $ 1. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
